acts.title: The Vigna Deposition — Monastery
acts.desc: The last monk of a dissolving monastery, Brother Tommaso, presents a sealed packet bearing the imperial chancellery device — a sworn deposition naming the courtiers who fabricated the treason charges against Pier della Vigna. The seal has never been broken. The packet has been under the monastery floor for fifty years. Insight DC 12: understand why it must reach the general record, not restricted access.
acts.passText: You understand the distinction before he explains it. Brother Tommaso nods and presses the packet into your hands. The seal is cold from the floor.
acts.failText: You ask about the contents. He explains them. The explanation takes longer than it should. The packet reaches your hands regardless.

acts.title: The Vigna Deposition — Road-Gate Courier
acts.desc: A papal courier checking correspondence from dissolved institutions stops the Fighter at the road-gate. He wants to catalogue the packet as dissolved-monastery property subject to papal inventory. The monastery never officially possessed the document — it was stored, not owned. Persuasion DC 13.
acts.passText: The courier notes 'personal document in transit, not institutional property' and releases the gate. He does this quickly, as if he has already forgotten the argument.
acts.failText: The courier flags the packet under provisional review. He releases it anyway after examining his authority — the flag travels with the document but does not stop it.

acts.title: The Vigna Deposition — Messer Fazio
acts.desc: The archive keeper is about to enter the document in restricted intake when a papal notary with two soldiers intervenes. The notary's authority covers documents from imperial chanceries; the deposition is testimony about imperial chancery conduct, not an imperial document itself. Persuasion DC 14; combat 2× AC 13 HP 18 if failed.
acts.passText: The notary listens to the distinction and withdraws. He writes something in his own ledger. The archive keeper opens the general intake.
acts.failText: Two soldiers. The archive keeper files it in restricted intake while the fight is happening. You retrieve it from restricted intake one day later through a procedural request. It has been filed — just in the wrong column, for now.

acts.title: The Vigna Deposition — Harbor Fire
acts.desc: A harbor fire blocks the direct route to the city registrar; the registrar closes at the second bell. Athletics DC 13 to navigate the blocked district in time.
acts.passText: You find the route through the warehouse district. The registrar is still at his desk when you arrive. The document is logged before he reaches for his closing seal.
acts.failText: You arrive at the third bell. The registrar has closed. You return at first light and file before the day's business begins. The stamp is dated the following morning.

acts.title: The Vigna Deposition — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. Sweelinck must decide between general and restricted filing. Insight DC 12: a specific precedent written on the wall behind the filing clerk gives Sweelinck legal cover for general intake. Recognize it before he asks.
acts.passText: You cite the precedent before he asks. Sweelinck looks at you for a moment. 'The divine verdict and the human record are separate registers,' he says. 'The human record is still owed the correction.' He files it in the general section.
acts.failText: Sweelinck finds the precedent himself, takes three minutes longer than he needed to, and files it in the general section anyway. The packet is in the archive.

acts.title: What Brunetto Asked — Notary's Estate
acts.desc: The late notary's estate, Florence. Executor Bernardo explains the Venetian dealer's advance knowledge and the authentication problem: only Ser Goffredo da Prato can confirm Brunetto's hand, and the dealer's guild right of first examination — filed tomorrow — gives him forty-eight hours to suppress the manuscript's publication. WIS DC 12: understand the forty-eight hour window before Bernardo explains it.
acts.passText: You understand the window: forty-eight hours from the dealer's formal examination request, filed tomorrow if you don't reach the archive first. Bernardo hands you the oilskin.
acts.failText: Bernardo doesn't explain the guild procedure. You learn it on the road when Giacomo cites it. But the manuscript is in your hands and the road to Ser Goffredo is clear.

acts.title: What Brunetto Asked — The Road North
acts.desc: The road to Ser Goffredo's villa. The dealer's representative Giacomo intercepts with a reasonable offer: his employer has better archive facilities in Venice. Without Ser Goffredo's authentication, the dealer's archive cannot accept the manuscript as genuine either. Persuasion DC 12.
acts.passText: Giacomo understands the argument: without Ser Goffredo's authentication in the chain, his employer's archive cannot accept the manuscript as genuine either. He turns his horse and rides back toward Florence.
acts.failText: Giacomo accepts your refusal but follows at a distance. He will have men at the road back. The manuscript continues to Ser Goffredo.

acts.title: What Brunetto Asked — Ser Goffredo's Villa
acts.desc: Ser Goffredo's hillside villa. He reads the manuscript for twenty minutes. He found the doubled 'l' in villano — Brunetto's characteristic hand. He asks the Fighter to read him the last line of the Tesoretto. Insight DC 12: know the last line.
acts.passText: You read the last line. He listens with his eyes closed. He says: 'Yes.' He signs without rushing. His name in two careful lines.
acts.failText: You read a line from the middle — close, but not the last line. He corrects you gently and recites it himself. Then he signs. The authentication is complete.

acts.title: What Brunetto Asked — Road Back
acts.desc: Two hours south of the villa, afternoon. Three of the dealer's hired riders in the vineyard section. Combat 2× AC 12 HP 20. The authentication leaf is sealed inside the oilskin — the riders do not know it is there.
acts.passText: Both riders are down. The oilskin is intact. Florence at nightfall.
acts.failText: They take the oilskin. But the authentication leaf is inside — they do not know it is there. The dealer will discover it when he opens the package. You have until morning before he can suppress the filing. Reach Ser Aldo before the dealer reads the leaf.

acts.title: What Brunetto Asked — Florence Archive
acts.desc: The civic archive's literary intake desk. Ser Aldo has been told about the dealer's interest. He is deciding whether Ser Goffredo's authentication — dated this morning — is sufficient for general literary classification. WIS DC 11: understand that a living-witness attestation dated today changes the procedural category.
acts.passText: Ser Aldo turns to the general ledger. 'Brunetto Latini, Tesoretto, continuation folios, authenticated by primary witness.' He stamps it. He takes the oilskin. He hands you Ser Goffredo's note: 'Maestro Brunetto would be glad.'
acts.failText: Ser Aldo enters it as disputed attribution pending review — the safest call. The manuscript is in the archive's custody, inaccessible to the dealer. In thirty days it will be reclassified when Ser Goffredo's status is confirmed.

acts.title: Francesca's Book — Malatesta Library
acts.desc: The Malatesta library, Rimini. Executor Matteo is cataloguing the estate. He is about to enter a specific volume as 'a French romance, unspecified' — an entry that makes it invisible to any later search. Francesca's niece Agnese has written a sealed account naming the book by its missing page. WIS DC 11: understand why the account changes the volume's legal category.
acts.passText: You take the folio before Matteo reaches for his seal. Agnese's name is on the outside. You understand what is inside without opening it.
acts.failText: Matteo pauses at the volume. You reach Agnese at the door just before the catalogue closes. She pushes the folio into your hands.

acts.title: Francesca's Book — Library Corridor
acts.desc: Matteo is reaching for his seal. The account changes the volume's legal category from estate property to material evidence, requiring him to hold it for registry review. Persuasion DC 12: explain this without accusing him of bad faith.
acts.passText: Matteo sets down his seal. He looks at the volume for a moment. 'Material evidence,' he says. He moves it from the French romance column to the contested pile.
acts.failText: Matteo is puzzled but not obstructive. He refers the question to his superior, who agrees after twenty minutes. The volume is held.

acts.title: Francesca's Book — Inheritance Registry
acts.desc: Rimini civic inheritance registry. The Malatesta heir's representative wants the account filed in supplementary correspondence — not primary evidence. Supplementary correspondence can be ignored; primary evidence cannot. Insight DC 12: determine what he is actually contesting.
acts.passText: You name what he is contesting — not accuracy but category. The clerk files it as primary evidence. The representative leaves.
acts.failText: The clerk accepts the argument eventually, filing it as primary evidence after consulting a procedural handbook. It takes twenty additional minutes.

acts.title: Francesca's Book — Harbor Road
acts.desc: The harbor road south. The heir's representative has a faster horse and the mail ship captain's ear. He is at the harbor when the Fighter arrives. Athletics DC 13: reach the captain before his version of what the Fighter carries is already lodged.
acts.passText: You reach the captain first. The account travels as primary evidence, not supplementary correspondence.
acts.failText: The representative reaches the captain first. His version is lodged. The captain reviews both accounts and accepts the original stamp as superseding. You continue.

acts.title: Francesca's Book — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. Sweelinck receives Agnese's account, endorsed by the Venice archivist's transit stamp. He reads it carefully, then reads the outside — the sealed folio of a woman who was fourteen and remembers exactly.
acts.passText: Sweelinck writes: 'First entry. Inventory Subversion Records — Objects Classified to Disappear. An unspecified French romance has no missing page.' He files it.
acts.failText: Sweelinck files it under Malatesta estate documents, cross-referenced to Francesca. The category is approximate but the account is in the archive.

acts.title: Bocca's Denial — Cavalryman's House
acts.desc: A small house on the Arno's south bank. Enrico di Giacomo, eighty-three, in a chair. He saw Bocca degli Abati's sword turn at Montaperti, September 4, 1260. He told a magistrate thirty years ago; not heard. He dictated the deposition this morning. 'The official history of Montaperti closes in three weeks. I need it in before the closing.' WIS DC 11.
acts.passText: The notary's seal is exactly level. Enrico's thumbprint is very clear. You take the deposition. He says: 'I have waited thirty years for a venue that counted. This is the last one.'
acts.failText: You take the deposition. Enrico is watching your hands as you put it away. He says: 'Carefully.' You carry it carefully.

acts.title: Bocca's Denial — The Street
acts.desc: Outside Enrico's house. An Abati family member steps in front of the Fighter. He is legally correct: testimony this old, from a partisan source, is not admissible without corroboration. But admissibility is for courts; the civic record is not a court — it receives documents. Persuasion DC 13.
acts.passText: He lets you walk past. He is still making his argument when you are gone.
acts.failText: He follows for two blocks before stopping. He is preparing a challenge through three separate procedures, but none of them are fast enough. The deposition continues.

acts.title: Bocca's Denial — Civic Archive
acts.desc: Florentine civic archive intake desk. The twenty-two-year-old intake clerk has been told all Montaperti additions need senior review — a committee that meets monthly, past the three-week closing date. But a dying declaration with a notary's seal, filed within twenty-four hours of dictation, is a specific category that bypasses the flag. Insight DC 11: find the category written on the wall behind the clerk's desk.
acts.passText: You point to the category on the wall. The clerk looks at it. He stamps the deposition directly into the current session. The flag does not apply.
acts.failText: You explain the category without pointing to the wall. The clerk accepts the argument and finds the category himself, which takes four additional minutes. The deposition is stamped.

acts.title: Bocca's Denial — Road to Venice
acts.desc: Road north. The Abati filed a challenge with the Venice territorial court; it will freeze the Florentine entry unless a corroborating document is filed in Venice within forty-eight hours. The notary has a second witness statement — a farrier who saw the same moment. Athletics DC 13: reach Venice in the window.
acts.passText: You arrive in time. The Venice court receives both documents. The Abati challenge is dismissed on procedural grounds. Enrico dies four days later — the timing was exact.
acts.failText: You arrive two hours past the window. The freeze is filed. A procedural counter-argument dissolves it the following day. The document is in the Venice record.

acts.title: Bocca's Denial — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. Enrico's notary sent a copy at Enrico's instruction, with a note: 'I am told there is an archive where things like this are filed in their own category. File it where it belongs.'
acts.passText: Sweelinck reads the thumbprint attestation. 'First entry. Dying Declarations — The Witness Who Could Not Speak in Any Venue That Counted.' He looks at you. 'The thumbprint is the signature of a man who had to speak with his body instead of his hand.'
acts.failText: Sweelinck files it under Montaperti, political history. He adds a cross-reference to Bocca degli Abati. The deposition is in the archive.

acts.title: The Pre-Schism Declaration — Private Consultation
acts.desc: A private room near the civic archive. Giacomo explains: his father's formal position statement is dated November 15, 1300 — three weeks before the Jubilee faction schism of December 8. The civic archive filed it as political abstention. The dates prove otherwise. The supplement closes today. WIS DC 11: understand immediately why the date is the entire argument.
acts.passText: You take the document and see the date without needing Giacomo to explain it. November 15. December 8. Three weeks. You move.
acts.failText: Giacomo explains the dates. He is precise and unhurried. You take the document and move.

acts.title: The Pre-Schism Declaration — Archive Reading Room
acts.desc: Supplement editor Messer Ottaviano: 'Three weeks is not a political issue.' He is making an editorial argument. The counter is archival: a pre-schism document and a post-schism abstention are different categories because the schism is what gives abstention its meaning. Persuasion DC 12.
acts.passText: Ottaviano holds the entry. He agrees to the category correction before closing the supplement.
acts.failText: Ottaviano holds the entry pending verification. He agrees to the category correction the following morning.

acts.title: The Pre-Schism Declaration — The Registry
acts.desc: Florentine civil registry. The clerk wants a contemporary witness attestation — a dated letter confirming the document existed before the schism. Giacomo has one: a correspondent's letter from two weeks before December 8 discussing the position statement in the context of 'factions that are beginning to form.' Insight DC 11: recognize the clerk needs the letter, not an argument.
acts.passText: You ask Giacomo for the letter before the clerk finishes his request. He produces it from his coat. The clerk stamps the correction.
acts.failText: The clerk explains what he needs. You send Giacomo back for the letter. He returns in twenty minutes. The clerk stamps the correction.

acts.title: The Pre-Schism Declaration — Road to Venice
acts.desc: The Venice territorial court jurisdiction. The White Guelph has filed a challenge that will succeed if it reaches Venice before the amended entry. Athletics DC 12: reach Venice before the petition window opens.
acts.passText: You file the corroborating documentation first. The Guelph petition arrives one hour later. The challenge is dismissed.
acts.failText: The petition window opens before you arrive. The challenge is reviewed. The corroborating documentation dissolves it. Two days are lost.

acts.title: The Pre-Schism Declaration — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. Giacomo's father is now in the biographical supplement as a pre-schism intellectual figure. Giacomo sent the original to Weimar as a case study with a note: 'The difference between my father and the souls in the Vestibule is a date. I want the date in the archive.'
acts.passText: Sweelinck writes: 'November 15, 1300. Three weeks before the schism. At that point the blank banner had not yet been raised. First entry. Pre-Schism Documents — The Distinction Between Principled Neutrality and Cowardice Is a Date.' He files it.
acts.failText: Sweelinck files it under Jubilee period documents. He adds Giacomo's note as a summary. The date is in the archive.

acts.title: Ugolino's Grandson — Pisa
acts.desc: Lorenzo's house, Pisa. Fra Bartolomeo's account names the specific civil treason charge terms Archbishop Ruggieri used against Ugolino — civil, not ecclesiastical, which meant no appeal to Rome. The Ruggieri heir died without a direct heir last month; the estate is in probate. File the transcript in the inheritance court before the probate window closes. WIS DC 11.
acts.passText: You take the transcript. Page three is where the charge terms are listed. The design is on page three.
acts.failText: Lorenzo explains the design in the civil treason charge. It takes him fifteen minutes. You take the transcript.

acts.title: Ugolino's Grandson — Inheritance Court
acts.desc: Pisan inheritance court. A Ruggieri estate representative objects: the transcript relates to events from 1289, seventy-five years before the current probate, and is collateral character evidence. The counter: the specific charges bear directly on whether the estate includes properties seized from the Ugolino family under those charges — foundational, not collateral. Persuasion DC 13.
acts.passText: The clerk enters the transcript as foundational. The representative leaves.
acts.failText: The representative keeps arguing. The clerk calls his superior. Twenty minutes later the transcript is entered as foundational.

acts.title: Ugolino's Grandson — Road to Florence
acts.desc: Pisa-Florence road. Three Ruggieri estate riders. The Fighter carries a certified copy — the original is in the probate file and cannot be suppressed. The writ the riders carry targets the original, which they do not have. Combat 2× AC 13 HP 22.
acts.passText: Two riders down. The third rider's writ is moot — it targets the original, which is in the probate file. The road is clear.
acts.failText: The riders delay you for twenty minutes before the legal situation becomes clear to them. The certified copy continues intact.

acts.title: Ugolino's Grandson — Florentine Archive
acts.desc: Florentine civic archive — the 1289 political history section. The archivist needs a contemporaneity confirmation: Fra Bartolomeo's admission records show he was in Pisa in 1289-1290 and transferred to Bologna in March 1290. The Dominican house is two streets away. Insight DC 12: recognize he needs the record, not an argument.
acts.passText: You go to the Dominican house and return with the admission record before the archivist's afternoon session ends. He stamps the civic record entry.
acts.failText: You explain Fra Bartolomeo's timeline verbally. The archivist listens, nods, and asks you to bring the record. You return with it within the hour.

acts.title: Ugolino's Grandson — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. Lorenzo sent a duplicate with a note: 'The mechanism Ruggieri used was the civil treason charge. The civil charge bypassed Rome. That was the design. The friar recorded the terms before the design was executed. I want the design in the archive.'
acts.passText: Sweelinck reads page three. 'The civil treason charge. Bypasses Rome. No appeal possible. The mechanism that makes a political murder look like a finding. First entry. Political Execution Records — The Judicial Mechanism That Concealed the Murder.' He looks at you. 'The design is in the archive. The Tower is in Dante.'
acts.failText: Sweelinck files it under Ugolino, Ruggieri, political history. He adds the charge terms as a summary note. The design is in the archive.

acts.title: The Cliff-Face Testimony — Cliff Base
acts.desc: A limestone cliff above the Arno valley. Stonecutter Rinaldo found carvings four years ago while quarrying — three decades of carved testimony: names, dates, fraudulent contract terms, carved where no court could erase them. The cliff face is fracturing. The rubbing is six feet of paper. 'Take it to whoever receives things that don't fit the categories.' WIS DC 11.
acts.passText: You take the oilskin tube. It is heavier than expected. You understand immediately why the categories failed him.
acts.failText: Rinaldo explains each failed channel — the commercial court, the civic archive, the lawyer. It takes twenty minutes. You take the tube.

acts.title: The Cliff-Face Testimony — Commercial Court
acts.desc: Pisan commercial court intake desk. A stonecutter's rubbing is not a primary document. But the commercial court has a historical commercial fraud category for documents that describe specific fraudulent clauses still in common use. Persuasion DC 12: argue the rubbing into the historical fraud category, not the artifact category.
acts.passText: The clerk enters it as historical commercial fraud documentation. Three of the fraudulent clauses are flagged as active variants.
acts.failText: The clerk refers to a supervisor. The supervisor agrees to the historical fraud category after examining the clauses. The rubbing is entered.

acts.title: The Cliff-Face Testimony — Defamation Opinion
acts.desc: A commercial lawyer hired by named merchants' descendants has issued a defamation opinion: carving names in stone is publication; the statute covers living persons; the merchants' heirs are living persons. But the named merchants are dead. The statute covers living persons at the time of the act, not their descendants. Insight DC 13: find the gap in the defamation opinion.
acts.passText: You identify the gap before the lawyer finishes his argument. He revises his opinion. The historical fraud entry stands.
acts.failText: The lawyer argues his position for forty minutes. You find a law dictionary and cite the temporal scope of the statute. He revises his opinion.

acts.title: The Cliff-Face Testimony — Harbor Customs
acts.desc: Venice harbor customs. The rubbing is six feet of paper in an oilskin tube — an unusual object under the assessable materials category. Rolling it out for inspection in the harbor air would damage it. Persuasion DC 12: satisfy customs without unrolling the rubbing in damaging conditions.
acts.passText: The customs officer accepts a written description of the content and the commercial court's intake record as sufficient. The tube is sealed through.
acts.failText: The officer insists on inspection. You negotiate a controlled unrolling in the customs shed. The paper survives; two edge marks are smudged.

acts.title: The Cliff-Face Testimony — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. Sweelinck unrolls the rubbing on the long table. He reads for a long time. He is reading the letters at the end — simple names with a single word after each.
acts.passText: Sweelinck writes: 'First entry. Testimony in Permanent Media — The Record Carved Where No Court Could Suppress It. He carved this where no one could erase it. Every institutional channel failed him for three years. The archive has no category problem with objects that outlasted their categories.' He files. He writes: questComplete.
acts.failText: Sweelinck files it under commercial history, Pisan fraud records. He notes the cliff face origin. The rubbing is in the archive.

acts.title: Phlegyas's Crossing Log — Florence
acts.desc: A dealer in ecclesiastical manuscripts — Elena — holds a folio: the administrative log of a boat crossing, Styx river, 1300. A weight differential notation and a marginal endorsement suggest a third party verified the transit as theologically legitimate. History DC 12: identify the format, explain the weight notation, and name what the marginal endorsement implies.
acts.passText: You identify the format, explain the weight notation, and name what the marginal endorsement implies: a third party verified the transit as legitimate. Elena names her price. You pay. You receive the Crossing Log Folio.
acts.failText: Elena's price doubles when she senses uncertainty. She folds the folio and locks it away. Two days later you may return; she loses no value waiting. You pay an additional 5gp on your next attempt.

acts.title: Phlegyas's Crossing Log — Rome
acts.desc: Rome. Fra Simeone at the ecclesiastical authentication office has the folio. He wants to authenticate the primary crossing log columns but dismisses the marginal endorsement as a later gloss. The endorsement is the document's historical core — the third-party verification that makes it archivable as theologically significant. Persuasion DC 13.
acts.passText: Fra Simeone examines both inks under a lens, writes two separate authentication notes — one for each hand — and dates them with a fifty-year margin placing both within the same century as Dante's journey. You receive Fra Simeone's Dual Authentication.
acts.failText: Fra Simeone agrees to authenticate the columns but dismisses the endorsement as a later gloss. His written opinion covers only the primary text. The archive will not accept the folio at full provenance grade without the endorsement analysis. You must spend two additional days finding a secondary expert.

acts.title: Phlegyas's Crossing Log — Palermo
acts.desc: Palermo. A noble family wants the folio to suppress prior archive entries about their ancestor's Styx crossing — they have a writ authorizing retrieval of their family's property from carriers. Combat 2× mounted retainers AC 14 HP 26.
acts.passText: Both retainers are down. The writ-holder folds his document and turns his horse. The road is clear. The folio is still in your pack.
acts.failText: You are unhorsed and the folio taken. The retainers leave you the authentication documents. Three days later a Genoese factor purchases the folio at auction; you recover it through a PAR contact before it leaves the island, at a cost of 15gp.

acts.title: Phlegyas's Crossing Log — Venice
acts.desc: Venice. Giacomo the Venetian archivist wants to verify the dissolution inventory from the Styx ecclesiastical commission before endorsing the crossing log — a certified copy of the Pisan inventory would establish the chain. Insight DC 12: recognize the dissolution inventory solution before he explains it fully.
acts.passText: You propose the dissolution inventory solution immediately. Giacomo nods and begins drafting his opinion while you arrange the Pisan certified copy by messenger. Three days later you have both. You receive Giacomo's Marginal Endorsement Analysis.
acts.failText: Giacomo declines to issue his opinion until the chain is complete. Without his endorsement, Weimar will accept the folio as interesting but not historically certified. You arrange the inventory copy; he endorses six days later.

acts.title: Phlegyas's Crossing Log — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. The Crossing Log Folio, Fra Simeone's dual authentication, Giacomo's marginal endorsement analysis. The archive receives the administrative record of a river crossing endorsed as theologically legitimate.
acts.passText: Sweelinck enters the folio under The Styx Crossing — Administrative Record of a Transit Endorsed as Theologically Legitimate. You receive the Archive Receipt: Styx Crossing.
acts.failText: Sweelinck files it under ecclesiastical transit records, 1300. The crossing log is in the archive.

acts.title: The Gate's Three Steps — Oltrarno Notary
acts.desc: Oltrarno district. Dying notary Bartolo di Vanni has a sealed folio — the parchment record of the three steps at Purgatory's gate (white marble, dark stone, blood-red porphyry) and the angel's procedures. He was a Vatican proceduralist; he filed it as a hypothetical procedural record. WIS DC 11: understand why a hypothetical procedural record is archivable as primary-source material.
acts.passText: You agree. Bartolo nods. You receive the Sealed Gate Entry Folio.
acts.failText: Bartolo explains the procedural filing distinction. You agree after his explanation. You receive the folio.

acts.title: The Gate's Three Steps — Rome Chancery
acts.desc: Rome chancery. The archivist wants to refer the folio to the theological commission — a committee that meets monthly and adds two months of delay. The folio is procedural, not theological; the chancery's intake for procedural ecclesiastical records does not require theological review. Persuasion DC 12.
acts.passText: The archivist issues a preliminary intake note and flags the Dominican registry match as the required next step. You receive the Chancery Preliminary Intake Note.
acts.failText: The archivist refers the folio to the theological commission. You retrieve it six weeks later with a commission stamp that says 'inconclusive — source unverifiable.' The archive will accept it at reduced provenance grade.

acts.title: The Gate's Three Steps — Palermo Convent
acts.desc: Fra Luca's mountain convent above Palermo. The Dominican registry confirms Fra Luca witnessed the folio's preparation — he is leaving for Calabria this morning. Athletics DC 14: climb to the convent before the door closes.
acts.passText: You arrive with five minutes to spare. Fra Luca is in the courtyard with his pack. You speak quickly and well. He listens, asks two questions, and writes his statement on the spot. You receive Fra Luca's Confirmatory Statement.
acts.failText: You arrive as the convent door closes. Fra Luca has gone. The prior will forward a message to Calabria, but his response takes six weeks. You continue with a delayed confirmation letter instead.

acts.title: The Gate's Three Steps — Venice
acts.desc: Venice. Scholar Caterina Miani is performing a comparative analysis — the folio's gate materials match three other procedural records. Insight DC 12: read her excitement correctly and ask the question that unlocks her full comparative analysis.
acts.passText: Caterina writes a full comparative analysis, including a section on the sword's material that argues the folio's source had experiential rather than literary knowledge of the intake procedure. You receive Caterina's Comparative Analysis.
acts.failText: Caterina writes a competent comparative note but does not address the sword discrepancy. The archive will accept the folio without that analysis, but Sweelinck's note will flag the unexplained detail as an open question.

acts.title: The Gate's Three Steps — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. The Gate Entry Folio, Fra Luca's statement, Caterina's comparative analysis. The archive receives the procedural record of the three steps as parchment, not theology.
acts.passText: Sweelinck enters the folio under The Gate of Purgatory — Procedural Record of the 1301 Intake, Source: Experiential. You receive the Archive Receipt: Gate Entry.
acts.failText: Sweelinck files it under Purgatorial procedures. The folio is in the archive.

acts.title: Matilda's River Registry — Oltrarno
acts.desc: Oltrarno district. Suora Margherita holds the River Registry Letter — the epistolary record of the Lethe and Eunoe river effects at the Earthly Paradise summit. She copied it from an older document before the copy was destroyed; she asks only that she be allowed to keep a copy of the Fighter's copy. WIS DC 11.
acts.passText: You agree. Suora Margherita makes her copy with practiced speed. She hands you the original. You receive the River Registry Letter.
acts.failText: You hesitate on the copy question. Suora Margherita makes the copy anyway, faster than expected, and hands you the original.

acts.title: Matilda's River Registry — Rome
acts.desc: Rome. Fra Pietro has the Augustine Confessions memory-theory citations that establish the theological framework for the Lethe effect. He is about to leave for an afternoon disputation. Persuasion DC 13: convince him to conduct the Augustine citation check now, before the disputation.
acts.passText: Fra Pietro sets down the Confessions, sends his student to cover the disputation, and spends the afternoon on the citation. By vespers he has a written analysis with specific text references. You receive Fra Pietro's Memory-Theory Analysis.
acts.failText: Fra Pietro defers to the next morning. You wait overnight in Rome. He produces his analysis at the first hour: complete but undated. The provenance chain is intact, the delay noted.

acts.title: Matilda's River Registry — Palermo
acts.desc: Palermo warehouse district. A factor holds a customs transit entry from 1302 that corroborates the river registry route. His family guards are blocking access. Combat 2× AC 12 HP 18.
acts.passText: Both guards are down. The factor leaves without further argument. The warehouse clerk copies the transit entry under his own notarial seal. You receive the Customs Transit Entry (1302).
acts.failText: You pay the factor's fee — 20gp — and he provides a certified copy under his family seal, which the archive will accept at reduced provenance grade.

acts.title: Matilda's River Registry — Venice
acts.desc: Venice. Ser Taddeo will perform a vellum analysis — he will provide correspondence access to the archive as a condition. Insight DC 12: recognize that the standard archive correspondence access policy automatically satisfies his condition.
acts.passText: You state immediately that the Weimar archive provides standard correspondence access to all researchers. Ser Taddeo nods, finishes his examination, and writes a full analysis including three parallel documents. You receive Ser Taddeo's Vellum Analysis.
acts.failText: You negotiate unnecessarily. Ser Taddeo is mildly annoyed. His analysis, while complete, does not include the comparative reference to the three parallel documents.

acts.title: Matilda's River Registry — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. The River Registry Letter, Fra Pietro's analysis, the customs transit entry, Ser Taddeo's vellum analysis. The archive receives the registry of what the Lethe river erased and what the Eunoe restored.
acts.passText: Sweelinck enters the letter under The Earthly Paradise — Registry of Lethe and Eunoe: What Was Erased and What Was Restored, Entry 1301. You receive the Archive Receipt: Matilda's Registry.
acts.failText: Sweelinck files it under Earthly Paradise documents. The letter is in the archive.

acts.title: Cacciaguida's Prophecy Register — Florence
acts.desc: Florence. Ser Niccolo Rancetti has a notarial register tracking the fulfillment of specific prophecies Cacciaguida made in the Paradiso. He will release the register for a nominal fee but requires the Fighter to agree to return a certified copy if the archive needs additional verification. WIS DC 11.
acts.passText: Ser Niccolo approves the statement, takes the nominal fee, logs the release, and hands you the register. You receive the Prophecy Fulfillment Register.
acts.failText: You are slow to agree to the copy condition. Ser Niccolo waits. You agree. He hands you the register.

acts.title: Cacciaguida's Prophecy Register — Rome
acts.desc: Rome. Fra Pietro again — this time for an Augustine citation establishing the theoretical basis for predictive vision. He is conducting a disputation. Persuasion DC 13: convince him to set it aside for the citation.
acts.passText: Fra Pietro sends his student to cover the disputation and produces the Augustine citation by mid-afternoon. He adds a cross-reference to three parallel prophecy records. You have everything before vespers.
acts.failText: Fra Pietro completes the disputation first. He produces the citation the following morning. The analysis is complete.

acts.title: Cacciaguida's Prophecy Register — Palermo
acts.desc: Palermo. A correspondence archive in a cellar holds the White Exile Network letters that corroborate twelve of Cacciaguida's predictions. The cellar access is on a narrow staircase blocked by fallen beams. Athletics DC 13: descend carefully to retrieve the correspondence without dropping the register.
acts.passText: You descend carefully, locate the correspondence cabinet, find the letter in the third folder from the left, and return without incident. The comparison confirms the match. Ser Rinaldo provides the certified copy. You receive the White Exile Network Letter.
acts.failText: You slip on the third step. The register is unharmed — you protected it — but you take 4 damage from the fall. The letter is retrieved; the comparison proceeds.

acts.title: Cacciaguida's Prophecy Register — Venice
acts.desc: Venice. Ser Bartolomeo is performing the comparative annotation — twelve of Cacciaguida's fourteen specific predictions documented in the register. He works alone in a designated room and has asked not to be interrupted. Insight DC 12: read his manner correctly — do not offer to help.
acts.passText: You wait in the designated room for three hours and twelve minutes. Ser Bartolomeo emerges with a full comparative annotation: twelve of fourteen predictions documented, two absent. You receive Ser Bartolomeo's Comparative Annotation.
acts.failText: You misread his manner as impatience and offer to help. He politely removes you from the comparison process and conducts it alone, producing a shorter summary. The summary is accurate but less granular.

acts.title: Cacciaguida's Prophecy Register — Archive
acts.desc: Weimar archive. The Prophecy Fulfillment Register, Fra Pietro's citations, the White Exile Network Letter, Ser Bartolomeo's comparative annotation. Twelve of fourteen predictions documented in primary sources. The archive receives the notarial record of a Paradiso prophecy's fulfillment.
acts.passText: Sweelinck enters the register under Cacciaguida's Prophecy — Notarial Record of Fulfillment, 1302–1321. He writes: questComplete. You receive the Archive Receipt: Prophecy Fulfilled.
acts.failText: Sweelinck files the register under predictive vision records, cross-referenced to Cacciaguida. The register is in the archive.
